symptomsGroup.title: Early Hormonal Shifts 💫
symptomsGroup.description: The first week marks the start of your menstrual cycle — your body is preparing for ovulation.

symptomItems.title: Mild Cramping ⚡
symptomItems.description: Some women experience light cramps as menstruation begins.

symptomItems.title: Fatigue 😴
symptomItems.description: Hormone fluctuations may make you feel more tired than usual.

symptomItems.title: Mood Swings 🎭
symptomItems.description: Shifting estrogen and progesterone can affect your emotions.

symptomsGroup.title: Ovulation Approaching 🌸
symptomsGroup.description: Your body gears up to release an egg — the time of highest fertility.

symptomItems.title: Increased Cervical Mucus 💧
symptomItems.description: Clear and stretchy mucus is common as ovulation nears.

symptomItems.title: Mild Pelvic Discomfort ⚖️
symptomItems.description: You might feel slight discomfort on one side — known as mittelschmerz.

symptomItems.title: Heightened Senses 👃
symptomItems.description: Smell and taste may be more sensitive due to hormonal surges.

symptomsGroup.title: Fertilization Stage 🧬
symptomsGroup.description: If conception occurred, a fertilized egg begins its journey to implant. Symptoms are subtle.

symptomItems.title: Mild Spotting 🩸
symptomItems.description: Some may notice light spotting due to implantation.

symptomItems.title: Tender Breasts 🤕
symptomItems.description: Hormonal changes might cause slight breast soreness.

symptomItems.title: Bloating 💨
symptomItems.description: Digestive slowdown begins — bloating may start.

symptomsGroup.title: Implantation Phase 🌟
symptomsGroup.description: The embryo implants into the uterus. hCG levels start rising — pregnancy may now be detected.

symptomItems.title: Nausea 🤢
symptomItems.description: Morning sickness may start — triggered by hCG rise.

symptomItems.title: Breast Tenderness 💥
symptomItems.description: Increased blood flow may make breasts feel heavier.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Urination 🚽
symptomItems.description: Hormonal shifts cause increased urination frequency.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 5 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Hormones surge and the embryo is forming — your body begins adapting.

symptomItems.title: Missed Period 📆
symptomItems.description: Often the first sign of pregnancy — your cycle pauses as hormones shift.

symptomItems.title: Breast Tenderness 🤕
symptomItems.description: Hormonal changes cause swelling and sensitivity in your breasts.

symptomItems.title: Fatigue 😴
symptomItems.description: Your body is working hard — it’s normal to feel very tired.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Urination 💧
symptomItems.description: Increased blood flow to kidneys results in more trips to the bathroom.

symptomItems.title: Mood Swings 🎭
symptomItems.description: Hormones can make emotions feel intense or unpredictable.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 6 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Hormones continue to rise — early symptoms become stronger.

symptomItems.title: Nausea 🤢
symptomItems.description: Morning sickness often begins this week — keep snacks handy.

symptomItems.title: Food Aversions 🚫🍗
symptomItems.description: Previously loved foods may now turn your stomach.

symptomItems.title: Bloating 🎈
symptomItems.description: Progesterone slows digestion, causing bloating and gassiness.

symptomItems.title: Heightened Smell 👃
symptomItems.description: You may notice certain smells seem stronger — even overwhelming.

symptomItems.title: Cramps & Spotting 💢
symptomItems.description: Mild cramping and light spotting can occur as the uterus adjusts.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 7 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: The embryo is growing rapidly — and symptoms reflect that.

symptomItems.title: Increased Saliva 💦
symptomItems.description: You might notice more saliva — a side effect of nausea.

symptomItems.title: Breast Veins More Visible 🫀
symptomItems.description: Increased blood volume makes veins more pronounced.

symptomItems.title: Digestive Changes 🍽️
symptomItems.description: Gas, heartburn, and slowed digestion can become more noticeable.

symptomItems.title: Acne Breakouts 💥
symptomItems.description: Hormonal shifts can increase oil production and cause pimples.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 8 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Hormones peak and your uterus continues expanding.

symptomItems.title: Morning Sickness 🤮
symptomItems.description: Nausea may worsen this week — eat bland foods and stay hydrated.

symptomItems.title: Tender Gums 🦷
symptomItems.description: Gums may swell and bleed more easily — keep brushing gently.

symptomItems.title: Excess Gas 💨
symptomItems.description: Hormones cause digestive slowdown and more gas.

symptomItems.title: Metallic Taste 🪙
symptomItems.description: You may notice a strange taste in your mouth.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 9 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Baby’s features are forming — your hormones are in full swing.

symptomItems.title: Breast Growth 🍈
symptomItems.description: Your breasts may feel fuller and begin enlarging.

symptomItems.title: Emotional Changes 😢😊
symptomItems.description: You might cry more easily or feel very up-and-down.

symptomItems.title: Headaches 🤕
symptomItems.description: Hormonal and circulation changes can trigger occasional headaches.

symptomItems.title: Fatigue Continues 🛌
symptomItems.description: Rest is still essential — your body is using more energy.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 10 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You’re nearing the end of the first trimester — symptoms may shift soon.

symptomItems.title: Round Ligament Pain 🤰
symptomItems.description: Stretching of ligaments can cause sharp or dull aches in your abdomen.

symptomItems.title: Visible Veins 🩵
symptomItems.description: Blood volume increases cause more visible veins, especially on breasts.

symptomItems.title: Mild Dizziness 🌀
symptomItems.description: Lower blood pressure can make you feel faint or lightheaded.

symptomItems.title: Mood Fluctuations 🎢
symptomItems.description: Mood swings may still come and go as hormones shift.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 11 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You're nearing the second trimester — some early symptoms may ease.

symptomItems.title: Less Nausea 🤞
symptomItems.description: Morning sickness may start to fade for some women this week.

symptomItems.title: Increased Discharge 🌊
symptomItems.description: More leukorrhea is normal — it protects the birth canal from infection.

symptomItems.title: Bloating & Gas 💨
symptomItems.description: Still common — hormonal effects on digestion persist.

symptomItems.title: Skin Changes 🌟
symptomItems.description: Your skin may become more oily or glow — thanks to hormones and blood flow.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 12 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby bump may start to show — and digestion begins shifting.

symptomItems.title: Visible Baby Bump 🤰
symptomItems.description: Your uterus is rising and may begin to show as a bump.

symptomItems.title: Constipation 🚽
symptomItems.description: Hormones slow down digestion — drink water and eat fiber.

symptomItems.title: Dizziness 🌀
symptomItems.description: Lower blood pressure can cause occasional lightheadedness.

symptomItems.title: Breast Changes Continue 🍈
symptomItems.description: Nipples and areolas may darken; veins become more visible.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 13 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You’ve entered the 2nd trimester — many women feel more energetic.

symptomItems.title: Increased Energy ⚡
symptomItems.description: Fatigue starts to fade for many as hormone levels balance.

symptomItems.title: Stretching Sensation 🧘
symptomItems.description: As the uterus grows, you might feel a stretching or pulling in your belly.

symptomItems.title: Nasal Congestion 🤧
symptomItems.description: Extra blood flow and hormones can cause stuffy nose or mild nosebleeds.

symptomItems.title: Visible Belly Line ➖
symptomItems.description: Linea nigra — a dark vertical line on the belly — may begin appearing.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 14 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Second trimester brings relief for many — but new changes begin too.

symptomItems.title: Rounder Belly 🫃
symptomItems.description: Your growing baby makes your bump more noticeable.

symptomItems.title: Varicose Veins 🟣
symptomItems.description: Increased blood pressure in veins can cause mild varicosities.

symptomItems.title: Leg Cramps 🦵
symptomItems.description: Muscle cramps, especially at night, can start in this trimester.

symptomItems.title: Skin Darkening 🌗
symptomItems.description: Melasma or blotchy dark spots can appear on cheeks or forehead.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 15 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Baby’s hearing develops — and your body continues to adapt.

symptomItems.title: Backaches 😣
symptomItems.description: A growing uterus can shift posture — causing back discomfort.

symptomItems.title: Mood Swings 💫
symptomItems.description: Hormonal surges may still cause emotional ups and downs.

symptomItems.title: Increased Appetite 🍽️
symptomItems.description: You may start feeling hungrier as your baby grows rapidly.

symptomItems.title: Fuller Hair 💇‍♀️
symptomItems.description: Hair may feel thicker due to slower hair loss during pregnancy.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 16 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You’re showing more visibly — and may start feeling new physical sensations.

symptomItems.title: Growing Belly 🤰
symptomItems.description: Your uterus is expanding — you may notice your belly starting to pop!

symptomItems.title: Shortness of Breath 🌬️
symptomItems.description: As your baby grows, your lungs may have slightly less room to expand.

symptomItems.title: Increased Discharge 🌊
symptomItems.description: More vaginal discharge (milky white) is normal — it helps prevent infection.

symptomItems.title: Fatigue 😴
symptomItems.description: You may still feel tired as your body works hard growing your baby.

symptomItems.title: Forgetfulness 🧠
symptomItems.description: Hormonal changes can affect memory and focus temporarily.

symptomItems.title: Back or Hip Aches 💆
symptomItems.description: Your ligaments are stretching — gentle movement or massage can help.

symptomItems.title: Swollen Feet 🦶
symptomItems.description: Extra blood flow and fluid retention can cause mild swelling.

symptomItems.title: Increased Appetite 🍽️
symptomItems.description: Your baby’s growth spurt may make you feel hungrier — eat nutritious meals.

symptomItems.title: Heartburn 🔥
symptomItems.description: Common as your uterus presses against the stomach — smaller meals help.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Urination 💧
symptomItems.description: Your uterus sits lower, adding pressure to your bladder again.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 17 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby is growing fast — and your body’s adjusting in kind.

symptomItems.title: Round Ligament Pain 🧵
symptomItems.description: Stretching ligaments can cause sharp or pulling sensations on either side of your belly.

symptomItems.title: Mild Swelling 💧
symptomItems.description: Swelling in hands, feet, and ankles may increase — elevate legs when possible.

symptomItems.title: Visible Veins 🩸
symptomItems.description: Increased blood volume makes veins more noticeable, especially on breasts and legs.

symptomItems.title: Itchy Belly 🪶
symptomItems.description: Skin is stretching — use gentle moisturizers to reduce dryness or itchiness.

symptomItems.title: Stronger Hair & Nails 💅
symptomItems.description: Hormones may lead to thicker hair and faster-growing nails.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 18 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You’re nearing the halfway point — more noticeable sensations begin.

symptomItems.title: Baby Flutters 🦋
symptomItems.description: You might feel your baby’s first movements, like bubbles or flutters.

symptomItems.title: Dizzy Spells 🌀
symptomItems.description: Standing up too quickly can make you feel dizzy — rise slowly.

symptomItems.title: Nasal Stuffiness 🤧
symptomItems.description: Hormones and blood flow may cause congestion or mild nosebleeds.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Hunger 🍔
symptomItems.description: With rapid baby growth, your appetite may increase again.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 19 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: As your belly expands, so do sensations like kicking and stretching.

symptomItems.title: Increased Baby Movement 🤸
symptomItems.description: Movements may feel more like soft kicks or rolls now.

symptomItems.title: Skin Sensitivity 🌞
symptomItems.description: Your skin may react more strongly to sun or products — stay protected.

symptomItems.title: Stretch Marks 🌈
symptomItems.description: You may begin to see light lines on the belly, breasts, or thighs.

symptomItems.title: Tingling Hands 🤲
symptomItems.description: Pressure on nerves can lead to tingling or numbness, especially at night.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 20 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Halfway there! You may notice both excitement and physical demands growing.

symptomItems.title: Stronger Kicks 👣
symptomItems.description: Baby’s kicks and jabs are now more distinct — especially when you're resting.

symptomItems.title: Lower Back Pain 🪑
symptomItems.description: Your center of gravity is shifting — support your posture and rest often.

symptomItems.title: Dry Eyes 👁️
symptomItems.description: Hormonal changes can reduce tear production — artificial tears may help.

symptomItems.title: More Frequent Urination 💦
symptomItems.description: Your uterus is pressing more on the bladder — restroom breaks are common.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 21 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby is getting bigger — and so is your bump!

symptomItems.title: Braxton Hicks Contractions 🤰
symptomItems.description: Mild, irregular tightening of your uterus as it practices for labor.

symptomItems.title: Dry or Itchy Skin 🧴
symptomItems.description: Stretching skin can feel dry — moisturizing can help.

symptomItems.title: Restless Legs 🦵
symptomItems.description: You might feel twitchy legs, especially when trying to sleep.

symptomItems.title: Gas and Bloating 💨
symptomItems.description: Hormonal changes slow digestion, leading to more gas.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 22 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby’s features are more defined — and your body keeps adjusting.

symptomItems.title: Swollen Gums 🦷
symptomItems.description: Hormones can make gums bleed more easily — brush gently.

symptomItems.title: Stretch Marks 🌈
symptomItems.description: You might notice new marks appearing as your belly expands.

symptomItems.title: Snoring 😴
symptomItems.description: Nasal passages may swell, leading to snoring while sleeping.

symptomItems.title: Mild Cramps ⚡
symptomItems.description: Growing uterus and ligaments can cause light aches or tugs.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 23 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You may feel more confident in your pregnancy body — and your baby is active.

symptomItems.title: Swelling in Ankles and Feet 🧦
symptomItems.description: Circulation changes can cause puffiness, especially after long days.

symptomItems.title: Mood Swings 🎭
symptomItems.description: Hormonal changes continue to affect your mood and emotions.

symptomItems.title: Leg Cramps 🦵
symptomItems.description: Sudden cramps, especially at night — stretch and hydrate well.

symptomItems.title: Thicker Hair 💇
symptomItems.description: You might notice fuller, shinier hair thanks to hormone shifts.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 24 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby is gaining fat — and you might feel more hungry too.

symptomItems.title: Increased Appetite 🍕
symptomItems.description: You may be hungrier — fuel with nutrient-rich snacks.

symptomItems.title: Pelvic Pressure ⚖️
symptomItems.description: Your growing uterus can create pressure lower in your belly.

symptomItems.title: Darkening Skin (Linea Nigra) 🟤
symptomItems.description: A dark line may appear on your belly — it’s totally normal.

symptomItems.title: Mild Dizziness 🌀
symptomItems.description: Blood pressure shifts may cause dizziness — sit or lie down if needed.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 25 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You're approaching the third trimester — strength and support are key now.

symptomItems.title: Backaches 🪑
symptomItems.description: Your posture and weight distribution are changing — try pregnancy-safe stretches.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Urination 💧
symptomItems.description: Baby’s position may cause more pressure on the bladder.

symptomItems.title: Insomnia 🌙
symptomItems.description: Difficulty sleeping may increase — find comfort with pillows and routines.

symptomItems.title: Clumsiness 🤕
symptomItems.description: A changing center of gravity can affect your balance — move slowly.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 26 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby’s eyes may start to open — and your symptoms may shift.

symptomItems.title: Swollen Hands 🤲
symptomItems.description: Mild hand swelling can occur — remove tight rings and stretch your fingers.

symptomItems.title: Braxton Hicks Contractions 🤰
symptomItems.description: Practice contractions may feel like tightness or pressure in your belly.

symptomItems.title: Tingling Limbs ⚡
symptomItems.description: Nerve compression can cause tingling in hands or legs — rest helps.

symptomItems.title: Increased Vaginal Discharge 🌊
symptomItems.description: A thin, white discharge is normal and helps prevent infection.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 27 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You're officially entering the third trimester!

symptomItems.title: Heartburn 🔥
symptomItems.description: Hormones relax digestive muscles, causing acid reflux — small meals help.

symptomItems.title: Itchy Belly 🧴
symptomItems.description: Stretching skin can become dry or itchy — moisturize often.

symptomItems.title: Shortness of Breath 🌬️
symptomItems.description: Your growing uterus may press against your lungs.

symptomItems.title: Emotional Changes 🎢
symptomItems.description: Hormonal shifts may cause anxiety or mood swings — self-care matters.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 28 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby’s brain is developing fast — and you might feel bigger changes too.

symptomItems.title: Lower Back Pain 🧍‍♀️
symptomItems.description: Postural shifts and baby’s weight may strain your lower back.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Urination 🚽
symptomItems.description: Increased pressure on your bladder returns — bathroom breaks may rise.

symptomItems.title: Breast Changes 🍼
symptomItems.description: Breasts may leak colostrum — a sign of preparation for nursing.

symptomItems.title: Leg Swelling 🦵
symptomItems.description: Standing too long or heat may worsen puffiness — elevate your feet.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 29 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You may feel more connected with your baby’s patterns and movement.

symptomItems.title: Pelvic Discomfort ⚖️
symptomItems.description: Baby may shift downward, causing pressure or soreness in your hips and pelvis.

symptomItems.title: Forgetfulness 🧠
symptomItems.description: Pregnancy brain can continue — jot things down to stay organized.

symptomItems.title: Constipation 🚽
symptomItems.description: Slow digestion and iron supplements may make bowel movements less frequent.

symptomItems.title: Increased Fetal Movement 🤸‍♂️
symptomItems.description: You might feel rolling, kicking, or hiccups — your baby is active!

symptomsGroup.title: Week 30 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your body and mind are preparing for labor — it’s okay to rest more.

symptomItems.title: Trouble Sleeping 🌙
symptomItems.description: Discomfort and an active mind can make sleep tricky — try a routine.

symptomItems.title: Fatigue 😴
symptomItems.description: You may feel tired easily — pace yourself and rest often.

symptomItems.title: Mild Swelling 🧦
symptomItems.description: Your feet and ankles may swell — compression socks can help.

symptomItems.title: Tight Belly Sensation 🤰
symptomItems.description: Your uterus continues practice contractions — monitor for patterns.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 31 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby is gaining weight quickly — and your body feels the effects.

symptomItems.title: Leaky Breasts 🍼
symptomItems.description: You may notice small leaks of colostrum — the first milk for baby.

symptomItems.title: Back Pain 🪑
symptomItems.description: Supportive pillows and better posture can ease your aching back.

symptomItems.title: Insomnia 🌙
symptomItems.description: Your growing bump and active baby might disrupt your sleep.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Urination 💧
symptomItems.description: Your baby is pressing more on the bladder — keep hydrated.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 32 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: With just 2 months to go, your body is preparing for labor slowly.

symptomItems.title: Braxton Hicks Contractions 🤰
symptomItems.description: Mild, irregular tightening of the uterus — your body is rehearsing.

symptomItems.title: Shortness of Breath 🌬️
symptomItems.description: Baby’s position might reduce lung space — take it slow.

symptomItems.title: Pelvic Pressure ⚖️
symptomItems.description: As baby drops lower, your pelvis may feel heavy or sore.

symptomItems.title: Stretch Marks 🌈
symptomItems.description: Rapid skin expansion may cause visible lines on your belly, hips, or breasts.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 33 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby is getting stronger — and your body’s gearing up for delivery.

symptomItems.title: Clumsiness 🫢
symptomItems.description: A shifting center of gravity can make movement awkward — be careful.

symptomItems.title: Vivid Dreams 🌌
symptomItems.description: Hormones and anticipation may bring strong, memorable dreams.

symptomItems.title: Leaky Bladder 💦
symptomItems.description: Sneezing, laughing, or coughing might cause slight leaks — pelvic floor exercises can help.

symptomItems.title: Lower Back and Hip Pain 🧍‍♀️
symptomItems.description: Relaxin hormone softens joints — support your body with rest and stretches.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 34 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby is almost full-term — things are getting real.

symptomItems.title: Swelling 😮‍💨
symptomItems.description: Feet, ankles, and even hands might swell — elevate and hydrate.

symptomItems.title: Nesting Instinct 🧹
symptomItems.description: You might feel a strong urge to organize or prepare your home for baby.

symptomItems.title: Fatigue 😴
symptomItems.description: Physical strain and mental preparation can leave you exhausted.

symptomItems.title: Hemorrhoids 🍇
symptomItems.description: Pressure on rectal veins may lead to discomfort — increase fiber and fluids.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 35 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your baby is almost ready to meet the world — and your body’s signs say so.

symptomItems.title: Pelvic Pain ⚖️
symptomItems.description: Baby’s head may be engaged, causing pressure in your pelvis or groin.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Bathroom Trips 🚽
symptomItems.description: Bladder pressure continues — go when you need to.

symptomItems.title: Backaches 🔙
symptomItems.description: Good posture and support can help ease the discomfort.

symptomItems.title: Trouble Sleeping 💤
symptomItems.description: Use pillows and find positions that ease pressure on your hips and back.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 36 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You're officially full term next week — the countdown begins!

symptomItems.title: Lightening ⚖️
symptomItems.description: Baby drops lower into the pelvis — you may breathe easier but feel pelvic pressure.

symptomItems.title: Increased Vaginal Discharge 💧
symptomItems.description: Thicker discharge or mucus plug may appear as labor nears.

symptomItems.title: Back and Pelvic Pain 🔙
symptomItems.description: Discomfort intensifies as joints loosen in preparation for birth.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Urination 🚽
symptomItems.description: Baby’s head presses more firmly against your bladder.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 37 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You’re full term — baby could arrive anytime!

symptomItems.title: Braxton Hicks Increase ⏳
symptomItems.description: Practice contractions may become more frequent and intense.

symptomItems.title: Pelvic Pressure 🔽
symptomItems.description: The baby may be 'engaged' — ready for labor.

symptomItems.title: Nipple Leaking 🍼
symptomItems.description: More colostrum may leak as your body prepares for breastfeeding.

symptomItems.title: Digestive Changes 🥴
symptomItems.description: Heartburn or nausea may return due to uterine pressure on your stomach.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 38 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You're nearing the finish line — every sign matters.

symptomItems.title: Increased Pelvic Pain 🦴
symptomItems.description: Baby's weight shifts more downward, affecting your hips and legs.

symptomItems.title: Loose Joints 🧍‍♀️
symptomItems.description: Your body produces relaxin to ease labor — which can make you feel wobbly.

symptomItems.title: Vaginal Pressure 🧷
symptomItems.description: Sharp, quick pain down low may signal baby’s head nudging nerves.

symptomItems.title: Fatigue 😴
symptomItems.description: Rest becomes challenging — try short naps when possible.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 39 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Baby is considered full term — you may notice signs of labor.

symptomItems.title: Mucus Plug Loss 🧼
symptomItems.description: A thick discharge or spotting could be the plug coming loose — labor may be near.

symptomItems.title: Cervical Dilation ⚖️
symptomItems.description: Your cervix may begin dilating — your provider may check at appointments.

symptomItems.title: Stronger Contractions 🤰
symptomItems.description: Timeable contractions may signal early labor — monitor their frequency.

symptomItems.title: Nesting Energy 🧹
symptomItems.description: A sudden burst of energy and urge to prepare is common now.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 40 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Your due date is here — stay calm and monitor signs of labor.

symptomItems.title: Contractions ⏱️
symptomItems.description: True labor contractions are regular, intense, and increase in frequency.

symptomItems.title: Water Breaking 💧
symptomItems.description: A gush or trickle of fluid could mean your amniotic sac has ruptured.

symptomItems.title: Pelvic Pressure 🔽
symptomItems.description: The baby's head presses even lower as labor nears.

symptomItems.title: Lower Back Pain 🔙
symptomItems.description: Persistent backache may be a labor sign — especially if rhythmic.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 41 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: You're past your due date — induction may be discussed soon.

symptomItems.title: Swelling 😮‍💨
symptomItems.description: Your feet and ankles may feel especially puffy — elevate when possible.

symptomItems.title: Frequent Monitoring 🩺
symptomItems.description: Expect more checkups to monitor baby’s health and movement.

symptomItems.title: Mood Swings 🎭
symptomItems.description: You may feel frustrated, anxious, or extra tired — totally normal.

symptomItems.title: Increased Discomfort 😵
symptomItems.description: Sleeping and walking may feel more difficult at this stage.

symptomsGroup.title: Week 42 Symptoms
symptomsGroup.description: Post-term pregnancy — your care team may recommend induction.

symptomItems.title: Very Low Baby Movements 🤱
symptomItems.description: Movement might slow, but should still be regular — track closely.

symptomItems.title: Increased Pelvic Pain 🦴
symptomItems.description: More pressure from baby’s position can strain joints and muscles.
